The Bible emphasizes having compassion for others, especially the vulnerable. A child is particularly vulnerable, so ignoring their cries might go against that teaching. I also think about the idea of neighborliness. In the Good Samaritan story, the Samaritan went out of his way to help someone in need, even though it was unexpected. Walking past without helping doesn't seem to align with that example. On the other hand, maybe the person has a reason for not stopping. Perhaps they're in a hurry, or they feel it's not their responsibility. But from a Christian standpoint, I think the emphasis is on taking action when we can help, especially when someone is in distress. I also remember that the Bible talks about not being indifferent to the suffering of others. Proverbs 21:13 says, "Whoever shuts their ears to the cry of the poor will also cry out and not be answered." That seems to suggest that ignoring others' needs can have consequences. So, putting it all together, I think from a Christian perspective, walking past a screaming child without helping would be considered wrong because it goes against teachings about compassion, helping others, and not being indifferent to suffering.
